sentences.text:
Complainant
 versus
Sh. Sandeep Kumar
S/o Sh Heera Lal
M/s Nanu Super Stores,
A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41
R/o F-7/327, Sultan Puri, Delhi-41 ... Accused
Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of th
e PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 01.08.2003, the Food Inspector (herein after referred as FI) Sh Sanjiv Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of 'Dal Arhar' a food article for analysis from accused Sandeep DA vs Sandeep Kumar Kumar at M/s Nanu Super Stores, A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Sandeep Kumar was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.

entities.text: Sandeep DA vs Sandeep Kumar Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sample consisted 1500 grams of Dal Arhar (ready for sale) taken from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration.
The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. Harish Kumar Ahuja, SDM/LHA.
The sample was taken after proper mixing the sample commodity with the help of clean and dry jhaba by rotating in all possible directions clockwise anti clockwise up and down several times.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting into three clean and dry bottles.
Each bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.

Notice was given to accused Sandeep Kumar and the price of sample was also given to him vide Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/
1 vendor receipt dated 01.08.2003.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.I were signed by accused Sandeep Kumar and the other witness Sh Brahma Nand, FA.

Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh Brahma Nand FA was joined as witness.
3.
One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 63/LHA/4903 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated.

The report of the Public Analyst is as DA vs Sandeep Kumar follows:
"The sample is Adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartarzine."
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused Sandeep Kumar was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Nanu Super Stores, A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41 at the time of sampling as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.
5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 08.12.2003 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(j)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.
6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 08.12.2003.
The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13(2) of the PFA Act.

Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a)
PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 and Rule 24 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

entities.text: Section 2(ia)(a)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 and Rule 24
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: DA vs Sandeep Kumar 7.
At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sanjeev Gupta, PW-2 FA Brahamand and PW-3 SDM/LHA Sh Harish Kumar Ahuja.
PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh.Harish Kumar Ahuja.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of 1500 grams of "Arhar Dal" from the vendor for analysis which was lying in an open gunny bag, bearing no label declaration, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three clean and dry glass bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C.
The vendor furnished photocopy of driving licence Ex.PW1/J.

Thereafter, on 04.08.2003 one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/
2

form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D and the remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received, according to which the sample was adulterated.
Thereafter PW-1 FI Sanjeev Kumar Gupta further investigated the matter and sent letter Ex.PW1/H to STO Ward No. 63 and received its reply stating that no such dealer registered in this ward.
After completion of DA vs Sandeep Kumar investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent.
The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/K.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/L was filed before the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/M alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/N which was received back undelivered.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel.
8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 03.09.2013 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence.
9. In defence, the accused examined a witness Anil Goel as DW-1 and placed on record bill Ex.DW1/A.
Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 12.05.2016 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
10. In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.

11.It is to be understood that the charge framed against the accused is for violation of section 2(ia)(a), (j) and (m) of the PFA Act read with Rules 23 and 29 of PFA Rules with respect to 'adulteration'.

Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific DA vs Sandeep Kumar nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be.

Section 2(ia)(j)
specifically deals with colouring matter which is present other than prescribed or is present beyond the prescribed limits of variability.

Section 2(ia)
(m) of PFA Act deals with situation where the quality or purity of an article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability.
12.
The commodity in the present case is Dal Arhar which is food grain and has to be tested as per the standards prescribed for food grains.
It is clear that this article falls in Item A.18.06.09 of Appendix B to the PFA Rules.
Both the analysts have applied the same standards to this product.
It is nowhere the stand of the accused that the food article does not fall under this head or that it falls under some other head.

Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/
3 13.
It is pertinent to note that both the chemical experts, PA and CFL, have found the presence of the synthetic colouring matter Tartrazine which is a totally prohibited item in the sample analysed.
On this point, both the reports are in conformity to each other and not at variance.

14. The defence taken by the accused is that he had purchased the dal from one Nihal Chand &
Company, Grave Merchant and Commission Agent, 3955, Naya Bazar, Delhi -6.

In order to prove this, he has called a partner from this firm Nihal Chand & DA vs Sandeep Kumar Company as a defence witness but this witness has not identified the bill Ex.DA on which the accused is relying for the purpose of benefit of warranty.

entities.text: Nihal Chand & DA vs Sandeep Kumar Company
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accused has placed on record the bill Ex.DA in the cross examination of PW-1 Food Inspector Sanjeev Kumar Gupta.
However, this witness has denied that the accused has shown this bill to him during investigation.
He further denied the suggestion that he refused to take the bill from the accused on the date of sampling.
15. It is pertinent to note that no such bill/invoice/cash memo of purchase of this Dal had been shown to the FI or the name of the supplier disclosed to him at the time of sampling.

Even if his stand is accepted that the FI had refused to accept the bill at the spot (though there is no evidence to this effect, except bald suggestions that were denied by the PWs), still nothing had prevented him from sending the documents to the PFA department at any time thereafter at the first available opportunity or even during the course of investigation.

No such stand was taken or name of the supplier disclosed even in letter Ex. PW-1/G given by the accused to the FI, so as to enable the FI to investigate the role of the supplier and to implicate or exonerate it.
When the complainant was not even informed about the particulars of the supplier, the accused cannot say that the FI did not verify the facts.
16. Be that as it may, it would be no defence available to the accused to claim that he was not the manufacturer of the commodity in question or that he was only a retailer using the same.
A seller or packer or distributor or manufacturer would operate in different fields and all of them can be held liable in their separate areas.
DA vs Sandeep Kumar Sale of adulterated food article is prohibited.
The definition of 'sale' under section 2 (xiii) is very wide which includes storing or exposing for sale as a retailer and even attempt to sell and also sale for analysis.

The only benefit which the accused can claim on this ground is under section 19(2) of PFA Act which would apply only if he is able to show that he had purchased the product against a warranty and had been selling the product in the same manner as purchased by him.
17. Even if the documents relied upon by him are accepted, that would not come to his rescue.
There is nothing to connect the lifted sample of dal arhar to the dal allegedly purchased through these documents bill Ex.DA.
The dal was lifted from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration.

Thus, there is nothing to show that the dal lifted from the restaurant was the same dal which the accused had allegedly purchased from DW-1 vide bill Ex.DA placed on record by him or any particular bill amongst these bills.

Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/
4 18.
Even otherwise, the bill produced by the accused do not qualify to give warranty to the accused under section 19(2) of the PFA Act.
For that, specific language is to be used as per Rule 12-A and as per Form-VIA, PFA Rules.

Reliance in this regard can be placed on M/s. Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86].

entities.text:
M/s. Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no batch number / code number or any other means to identify the dal sold to be the one lifted.
Again, the bill/invoice should carry a warranty in the prescribed language.
But in this case, the bills mention a Note to the effect that "We are not responsible for the goods after delivery from our shop."

Without commenting on the correctness of the language and or legality of DA vs Sandeep Kumar such claim of evasion of liability under the PFA Act, it is certain that the warranty as prescribed by Rule 12-A and Form VI-A of PFA Rules is not there on the bill.

19. Further, it is to be understood that the benefit of warranty under section 19(2) of PFA Act would be available only when there is a written warranty from the supplier/seller in addition to the fact that it has been sold in the same condition as was purchased.
Both the conditions have to be fulfilled simultaneously.
There is further no evidence to the effect that the dal was in same state or condition when sold/used.
There is no witness who could depose that the dal lifted from possession of the accused was in the same condition as was purchased though the bill in question.
The accused has not examined himself as defence witness to prove that he has purchased this dal from some other person and was selling it in the same condition.
And therefore, even the complainant did not get any opportunity to cross-examine any such witness on the said claimed stand.
Thus, even the benefit of warranty cannot be extended to the accused in this case.

20. The case in hand would be therefore covered under section 2(ia)
(a) of PFA Act as there is evidence to show that it was not of the nature, substance or quality which it is purported to be as per PFA Rules.
The case would fall under section 2(ia)(j) as there is presence of colour which is not permitted in this article.
Violation of section 2(ia)(j) is punishable under section 16(1A) and violation of section 2(ia)(a) is punishable under section 16(i)(a) of PFA Act.
But being graver offence, conviction can be under section 16(1A) of PFA Act.
DA vs Sandeep Kumar 21.
Having said so, it can be said that the complainant / prosecution has been able to establish its case and prove the guilt of the accused beyond the shadow of reasonable doubt.

It has been proved that the accused had sold adulterated food in violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (j) of PFA Act read with Rules 23, 28 and 29 of PFA Rules, and has committed the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act.
22. Thus, the accused is held guilty and convicted for the offence punishable under section 16(1A) of the PFA Act.

Let the matter be listed for arguments on sentence Announced in the open court this 2nd day of July 2018 SAMAR VISHAL ACMM-II (New Delhi), PHC DA vs Sandeep Kumar Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/
